import os,re,json,collections,itertools
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
I2,O2=G['Demo pair 2 input'],G['Demo pair 2 output']; N2=22
# anti-diagonal structure: count of color 5 per anti-diagonal. Pattern suggests bands grow by one cell per two diagonals, but with wrap/step changes at diag 8/9 then constant. Look at actual O2 values along each anti-diagonal to see exact shape.
for s in range(0,43):
    vals=[O2[i][j] for i in range(N2) for j in range(N2) if i+j==s]
    # print only where NOT all same, or summarize: set and first value
    if len(set(vals))==1: continue
    print(s,vals[:6],'...',len(set(vals)))

import os,re,collections,itertools,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
def strip(I):
    row=I[0]; nz=[c for c in row if c!=0]
    # find contiguous nonzero run starting at first nonzero
    st=row.index(next(c for c in row if c!=0)); en=row.rindex(next(c for c in reversed(row) if c!=0))
    return row[st:en+1]
for nm in ['Demo pair %d'%k for k in range(1,8)]:
    I=G[nm+' input']; O=G[nm+' output']
    C=strip(I); p=len(C); N2=len(O)
    ok=all(O[i][j]==C[max(i,j)%p] for i in range(N2) for j in range(N2))
    print(nm,p,len(C),ok)

def load():

Interesting. Outputs are not 2x the input in size! Demo 1: input 14x14, output 28x28 — wait yes it is 28x28 (N=2n). But my solve predicted row 0 all 4s but actual row 0 is all 4s... wait pred row 0 = [4,1,...] that's wrong; actual row 0 is all 4s. Hmm, O row 0 all 4s, and O row 1 = I[1] extended. So O[i][j] = I[min(i,j)][min(i,j)]? For i=1,j=1 → I[1][1]=1 ✓; for i=0,j=1 → I[0][0]=4 ✓. That IS diag min with no mod. Earlier attempt "diag min" failed because I used min(i,j) without %n... but demo 3 earlier "min-cyc False". Actually earlier failure was due to buggy code mixing indices. Let me just test O[i][j]==I[min(i,j)][min(i,j)] directly now.

Demo pair 5 row 0 of output starts 6,8,5,... which equals I's row pattern starting at col 5? Output rows shift by one each row going down-left. Yes looks like a staircase: each row is shifted left by one relative to previous? Look at demo 7: output row r vs row r+1 shifts by one left... Actually pattern: O row i = concat(I row k cyclic?) Let's just check O[i][j]==I[min(i,j)][?]... In demo 3, output is periodic extension: columns j< n follow I, and beyond n continue pattern with period n? Demo 3: output row 0 = [2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,...] = I row 0 tiled periodically. And diagonals: cell (i,j)=I[j%12]? Check demo3 cell(11,11): I[11][11]=0? Input row 11 all zeros; output row 11: all 5s? Output row 11 = [5]*24 except last two 5,4... wait printed row 11 ends "5,2,4,5,1". Hmm output row 11: from print: `[5,5,...,5,2,4,5,1]`? It shows ...,5,2,4,5,1 at end. That's I tiled? I row 0 tiles horizontally: period 12 → pos 10,11 = 0,0 but output has 5,1. So not plain tiling.

Actually this is a triangular tile: output[i][j] = I[min(i,j)][min(i,j)] but with wraparound... In demo 3, cells where min(i,j)>=12 use wrap? min(i,j) max is 23, so min≥12 never happens (max index 23→ but n=12, min≤11 since both ≤23... no min can be up to 11 only? min(i,j) for N=24: max min = 11 when i=j=11... actually min(i,j) up to 11). So min(i,j) always <12! Then O[i][j]=I[min(i,j)][min(i,j)] gives row 0 all I[0][0]=2 — but output row 0 = [2,4,5,1,...]. Not that.

Look again: output seems like each row i is I row i cyclic-shifted? Demo 7: output row 0 = I row 0 shifted by 0? I row 0 = [0,0,0,0,7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2]; O row 0 = same. Row 1 same. Row 2: O row 2 differs at positions 18-23: [...,7,7,7,7,7] vs I has 7,2,2,7,2,2. Row 2 of O: [7*8,2,7,2,2, then 7,7,7,7,7,7] i.e. tail becomes 7s. Hmm.

Alternative: think of input as composed of horizontal bands/blocks. The transformation appears to be: extend the pattern downward-left as a 2x-tiled structure where each block repeats? Output height = 2n, width 2n. Structure: O[i][j] = I[(i + something)? ...]. Consider O[i][j] = I[((i - j) ? )]. Try O[i][j] = I[j%12][(j-i)%12]? That's a diagonal shift. Check demo 7 row 0: j=i=0.. → I[j][0] = column 0 = all 0s. No.

Maybe output is built by placing copies of I scaled/shifted in quadrants like a fractal: BL quadrant == I (verified for demo 1), TR == identity too. TL and BR unknown. In demo 3, TL region: rows 0-11 cols 0-11 = I itself (rows identical to I rows 0-11!). Row 12+ in TL? Output row 12: [5,5,...] — TL row 12 = output row 12 cols 0-11 = all 5s? Printed: row12 = [5]*... yes mostly 5s. And BR: rows 12-23, cols 12-23.

Compare: maybe O = 2x2 arrangement where each quadrant is I transformed: TL=I, TR=I flipped somehow, etc. Demo 1: TR==I exactly, BL==I exactly. TL and BR are zero-filled regions? Demo 1 I has no zeros; output TL row 14+: [4]*14 then shifting values 1,4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4... hmm TL row 14 = first 14 entries of row 15 of I? I row 15 doesn't exist. Actually I rows: row 13=[1,4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4]. TL row 14 = [4]*14 then continues... printed TL row 14: "[4,4,...,4,1,4,2,9,...]" — that's like the bottom-right anti-diagonal band continuing. Interesting: TL row 14 = row 14 of some extended structure. Maybe the full picture: consider infinite staircase matrix S where S[i][j]=I[min(i,j)][min(i,j)]; output is a window? No—output rows contain varied sequences.

New idea: O[i][j] = I[a*i + b*(j-i)...]. Better: examine O as composed of blocks: O[i][j] might equal I[k][l] where k,l derived via k=min(i,j)? already fails. Try k=min(i,j) with clamping/wrap differently: maybe k=(min(i,j)) but the value comes from I row k shifted... 

Let's compute numerically. Search: O[i][j]==I[p(i)][q(j)]? For demo 3: row 0 of O = I row 0 tiled. Row 1 = I row 1 tiled? I row 1 = [4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0], O row 1 = [4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1,6,...]. Position 10,11: I=0,0; O=2,4. Positions 10-23: 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4 — that's I row 0 shifted. So O[1][10..] = I[0][?]. Specifically O[1][10+k] = I[0][(k+2)%12]: k=0→I[0][2]=5? O[1][10]=2. Hmm I[0] rotated: sequence 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5 then repeat: matches O[1][10:] = 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4? O[1][20..23] = 5,2,4,5? printed ends "...,5,2,4,5,1" at positions 20-23: 5,2,4,5? Let me count: O row 1 given: [4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1] positions 0-23. So O[1][10:]=[2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4] length 14 wrapping → O[1][10]=2, [11]=4, [12]=5, [13]=1,... consistent with period-12 sequence starting at offset 2 of I row 0: I0 = [2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0]; take I0 shifted: seq starting at index 2: 5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0,2,4 — no, O has at 10: 2,11:4. Sequence at 10: 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5 repeating with period 10? From pos 10: 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5 | then pos 20: 5,2,4,5,1 → positions 20-23 = 5,2,4,5. If period were the 10-length block B=[2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5], pos 20 = B[0]=2, but actual 5. Block of length 12 from I0 without zeros: [2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5] then wraps to I0[0]=2,I0[1]=4 → pos 20=B[0]=2? actual 5. Hmm so maybe pos 20 = I0[9]=5? B has 10 elements; pos 20 ≡ pos 8 mod 12 → I0[8]=7. Actual O[1][20]=5. ≡ pos 9 → I0[9]=5 ✓. pos 21 ≡ 10 → 0, actual 2 ✗. Unless zeros in I are filled by next nonzero... pos 21=2, pos 22=4, pos 23=5, pos 0=4. Pattern pos 20-23: 5,2,4,5 | pos 0-3: 4,4,5,1. Combined tail 20-23 + 0-3: 5,2,4,5,4,4,5,1. Compare with I0 rotated: I0 has ...7,5,0,0 then 2,4,... The zeros replaced by continuation: after 7,5 comes (wrapping) 2,4,5? Actually zeros in I0 at 10,11 get replaced by values from further along: 2,4? then pos 12 would be I0[0]=2 but O[1][12]=5. Hmm pos 12 = 5 = I0[9]. pos 13 = 1 = I0[3]. pos 14=6=I0[4]. pos 15=1=I0[5]. pos 16=7=I0[6]. pos 17=1=I0[7]. pos 18=7=I0[8]. pos 19=5=I0[9]. pos 20=2=I0[0]?? actual 5. Wait recount: O row1 list: indices: 0:4,1:4,2:5,3:1,4:6,5:1,6:7,7:1,8:7,9:5,10:2,11:4,12:5,13:1,14:6,15:1,16:7,17:1,18:7,19:5,20:2,21:4,22:5,23:1. So from 10 onward: 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1 — pure period-12 starting at index 10 with value 2 = I0[0]. So O[1][j] = I0[(j-10) mod 12]? j=10→0→2 ✓, j=22→12→5? I0[0]=2 ✗ actual 5. j=22: (22-10)%12=2→I0[2]=5 ✓! j=23: 3→I0[3]=1 ✓. j=20: 0→2 ✓ (I miscounted earlier). Great: O[1][j] = I[row?][(j + off) mod 12] with row depending on i.

So generally: O[i][j] = I[r(i)][c(j)] with r,c depending on i,j via staircase. Row 0: O[0][j]=I0[j] for j<12 and continues: O[0][12..23]=2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4 — same period-12 sequence! So O[i][j] = I0[(j + s(i)) mod 12] where s(i)=? Row 0: s=0; row 1: s=-10≡2 mod 12? (j-10). Row 2: O row 2 = I0? printed: [4,4,5,...,0→?]. Row 2: [5? no: row2=[4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0? no]. Printed row 2: [4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5, 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1] wait printed row index 2: "[4, 4, 5, 1, 6, 1, 7, 1, 7, 5, 2, 4, 5, 1, ...]"? Looking at printout line 3 (index 2): [4, 4, 5, 1, 6, 1, 7, 1, 7, 5, 2, 4, 5, 1, 6, 1, 7, 1, 7, 5, 2, 4, 5, 1]. Hmm same as row 1? No wait that's row index 2? Lines: 0: [2,4,...], 1: [4,4,...], 2: [5,5,5,1,...]. Let me recount from output: line0 = [2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0|tiled], line1 = [4,4,5,1,...], line2 = [5,5,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1,...]. OK.

So pattern: O[i][j] = I[a(i)][b(j)]? Check line 2 vs I row 2 = [5,5,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0]. Line 2 positions 0-9 = I row 2 exactly. Positions 10-23: 2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4 — same as before: I row 0-ish sequence. So horizontally: the right part uses a different row of I, wrapped. Vertical: line i vs line i+1: line 0 and line 1 share content with different offsets... This smells like O[i][j] = I[min(i, something)][...]. Actually simplest unified form: O[i][j] = I[u][v] where u = min(i, j-th-related)? 

Check hypothesis O[i][j] = I[min(i,j)][min(i,j)] for small: O[1][1]=I[1][1]=4 ✓. O[1][2]=I[1][1]=4 ✓. O[1][3]=I[1][1]=4, actual 1 ✗. No.

Hypothesis: O[i][j] = I[min(i,j)][k] where k = j - something... Try O[i][j] = I[a][b] with a=min(i,j)+? Actually observe: within output, cell (i,j) seems determined by min(i,j) and (i-j) parity? Let's do it computationally: find formula via matching: for each cell, which (I row, I col) does it come from, and see relation between (i,j) and (r,c). Since output is periodic in both directions likely: O[i][j] = I[(r(i))][ (c(j)) ]? Check demo 3 row 0 vs other rows: row 0 uses I row 0 everywhere (both halves). Row 1: left half uses I row 1? Left half of row 1 = [4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5] = I row 1 ✓. Right half uses sequence starting 2,4,... = I row 0 from index 0. Row 2: left = I row 2; right = starts 2,4 (I row 0 idx 0). Row 12+ rows: e.g., row 13 = [1]*14 + [6,1,7,1,7,5,2,4,5,1,6,...]: left half = I row 3? I row 3 = [1,1,1,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0] — left half row 13 = [1]*14 all ones ✗ (I row 3 has 6 at index 4). Hmm row 13 left = all 1s. I row 7? All 1s? I row 7 = [1]*9+[1,7,5...] no. Rows of I that are all 1: none fully; row 3 first 4 are 1. Row 13 left: 14 ones. Hmm.

Wait maybe vertical also shifts: O[13][j] = I[(13 + s) % 12][(j + t) % 12] for some shifts? I row with all-ones: none. Row 13 left all 1s though. Unless left half uses a different mapping: maybe O[i][j] = I[(i+j) or (i-j) stuff]. Let me think of the whole thing as: O = some function g over Z^2 with O[i][j] periodic mod 12 in both directions, and on the 12x12 base grid O[i][j] = I[?][?]. Base grid O[0..11][0..11]: compare to I: O row 0 = I row 0? O[0][0]=2=I[0][0], O[0][1]=4=I[1][0]! O[0] = [2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0] which equals I column 0 read down: I[:,0] = [2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5,0,0] ✓! So O[0][j] = I[j][0]... i.e., transpose-ish: O[i][j] = I[min(i,j)][?]. O[0][j]=I[j][0]: for i=0, min=0, value I[j][0]. Hmm.

O[1][j]: left half = I[1]?? O[1][0..9]=[4,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5]=I row 1 ✓. O[1][10..]=2,4,5,...=I row 0. So O[1][j]=I[min(1,j)][something]. For j≥1: min=1 but values come from row 0. So not min.

Alternative view: O[i][j] = I[j'][i'] where... consider map (i,j) → (a,b) with a=min(i,j)? For cell (1,10): a=1, value from I row 0. (0,10): a=0, value I row 0 idx 10=0, but O[0][10]=0 ✓! (1,10): I[0][10]=0 ✗ (actual 2). Hmm.

Try: O[i][j] = I[(i+j) or (j-i)]... (1,10): j-i=9, I[9] = [5,...] no.

Let's reconsider: maybe the rule is about the input's own structure. Each input is a set of colored rectangular staircase blocks anchored bottom-right. The outputs look like the blocks themselves tiled periodically across the whole 2N canvas. E.g., demo 3: blocks: the staircase "2,4,5,1,6,1,7,1,7,5" shape occupies top-right area; zeros fill elsewhere. The output fills the entire canvas with the pattern of blocks repeated/tiled.

Actually notice demo 6 output: O[i][j] = pattern of period 4: [3,9,5,5] repeating in both directions, with staircase modification. Demo 7: period pattern [7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2] with modifications. These look like: the base pattern P (the non-zero part of I arranged along anti-diagonal direction?) tiled everywhere, and the zero regions of I become... In demo 7, the non-zero block in I spans rows 0-7, cols 4-11. Output covers whole 24x24 with the same block structure repeated every 8 rows/cols? Check O rows 8-15, cols 0-7: printed rows 8-15 cols 0-7: row 8: [7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2] same as row 0! Row 9: same. Row 10: [7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2,...] same. So vertically the pattern repeats every 8. Horizontally: row 0: cols 0-7 = [7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2], cols 8-15 = [7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2], cols 16-23 = [7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2]. All same! So O is literally periodic tiling of an 8x8 block: [[7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2],[7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2],[7,7,7,7,2,7,7,7],[7,7,7,7,2,7,2,2],[...]] wait but the input has variations (row 2 ends 7,7 instead of 2,2; row 8 ends 2s). Hmm input row 2: [...,7,7,7,7] at cols 8-11, but tiled would give row 2 cols 8-11 = [7,7,7,7]? Tile block row 2 = [7,7,7,7,2,7,7,7] → cols 8-11 = [2,7,7,7]? No: tile row index 2 = [7,7,7,7,2,7,7,7], cols 8-11 = tile cols 0-3 = [7,7,7,7]. Input row 2 cols 8-11 = [2,7,7,7]. So input ≠ one clean 8-block.

Hmm, actually maybe simpler: the whole 28x28 demo 7 output equals input tiled 2x2 WITH modifications in the zero quadrants? Check: is O[i][j] for i,j in [0,13) x [0,13) equal I? Input top-left 13x13 mostly zeros; output top-left has 7s and 2s. No.

OK step back: the real structure might be: O is constructed by taking the input's non-zero pattern and stamping it repeatedly at all positions where it fits, filling everything. The inputs consist of colored rectangles arranged in a staircase (each color forms an L/staircase anchored bottom-right corner). Rule guess: tile the plane with the minimal bounding "staircase tile" such that the original input appears at its natural position, filling remaining area with the periodic extension — the zero areas in input are where the tile doesn't cover, and the output fills them with the periodic continuation.

Test on demo 3: I's non-zero region: rows 0-9, cols 0-9 (the staircase block of colors 2,4,5,1,6,7), plus row 0? The block: it's the 10x10 staircase. Tiling with period 10: output would be O[i][j]=I[i%10][j%10] restricted... but I has zeros inside? I rows 10,11 are all zero (below block). O rows 10,11: row 10 = [2,2,2,...] all 2s?! O row 10 printed: [2,2,2,2,...,2,4,5,1,...]. Hmm O row 10 = all 2s then 4,5,1,... from col 11. Under "tile I with period 10": O[10][j]=I[0][j%10]: j=0→2 ✓, j=1→4? actual O[10][1]=2 ✗.

Ugh. Let me look at actual O rows near boundaries more carefully with code instead of eyeballing. Also note demo 1: O rows 0-13 = I rows 0-13 extended: O row 14 = [4]*14 + [2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4]... which equals I row 13? I row 13 = [1,4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4]. O row 14 cols 14-27 = 2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4 = I row 13 cols 1-12? I row 13[1:]=4,2,9,... no: I row13 = [1,4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4]; O row14 tail = 2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4 = I row 13 rotated by 2? I row13 shifted: [2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4,1,...]. O tail is 12 values: 2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4. Rotated I row13 starting at index 2: [2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4] ✓ exactly (length 12, then would wrap to 1,4...). So O row 14 = [4]*14 + rot2(I row 13)[0:14].

And O row 13 (first 14) = I row 13, then continues 2,9,7,... same tail. So O row 13 = I row 13 + tail(rotated). O row 15 = [1]*14 + tail starting at index? O row 15 = [1]*14 + [2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4] — same tail as row 14! And row 16: [1]*15 + [4,2,9,7,...]: tail starts at I row 13 index 1? I row 13[1:]=4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4... O row16 tail after 15 ones: 4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4 → matches I row 13 from index 1.

So rows 14+ follow: O row i (i≥14) = [I[13][0]]? no... row 14: 14 fours then rot2-tail. Hmm alternatively: think of O as the staircase continuing downward-left: the input's staircase descends to the bottom-right corner; output continues the staircase past the input's edge, wrapping around toroidally. I.e., O is the input's pattern extended infinitely in all directions (toroidal wrap), then cropped to 2N×2N?

For demo 1: infinite extension: cell (i,j) in the extended pattern = I[(i + k) ... ]. The staircase: I[i][j] = I[min(i,j)]? No: I[i][j] = I[i][min(i,j)]? Check I row 1: [1]*13 + [4]: I[1][j] = I[1][1] for j≥1? I[1][1]=1, I[1][13]=4. I[1][j]=I[1][min(j,13)]... trivially true since row 1 constant except last. Row 2: [9]*12+[1,4]: I[2][j] = I[2][min(j,12)] = 9 for j≤12, 1 for 13, 4? j=13: min=13 >12, value 4? Hmm I[2][13]=4, I[2][12]=1. So I[2][j] = I[2][j] for j≤12 constant 9, then 1,4. Actually the rule: I[i][j] = D[min(i,j)] where D is diagonal? I[2][2]=9=D[2] ✓, I[1][1]=1=D[1], I[1][13]=4: D[min]=D[1]=1 ✗. So not simple.

The structure: I is built from blocks: color c occupies rectangle [r0..r1] × [c0..c1] forming staircase. I[i][j] for j ≥ threshold(i) follows sequence along anti... Let me model: for demo1, I[i][j]: for j < f(i): D[i]; else: depends on j. Row 12: [4,4,2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4]: threshold: j=0,1: 4,4. j=2:2, j=3:9,... So each row: prefix of length p(i) then staircases. Column-wise similar. Actually I[i][j] = D[min(i,j)] except where the "staircase tail" overrides? I[1][13]=4: D[min]=D[1]=1, but actual 4. I[2][13]: D[2]=9, actual 4. Hmm.

Think of it as: I is generated from sequence D = diag: [4,1,9,2,8,7,6,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,7,9,...]. I[i][j] = D[min(i,j)] for most cells, but cells below/left of the diagonal band differ. I[2][13]=4 = D[?]. Where's 4 in D: index 0. I[1][13]=4=D[0]. I[3][13]? I row 3 = [2]*11+[9,1,4]: I[3][13]=4=D[0]. Hmm many cells map to D[0].

Actually maybe: I[i][j] = D[min(i,j)] where the staircase means the "effective index" decreases going down-left? Like O extends the pattern: for the OUTPUT, define for all i,j: O[i][j] = D[g(i,j)] for some g, where D is the cyclic diagonal sequence of the input, and g encodes distance from the anti-staircase boundary.

Given time constraints, better approach: extract the rule empirically per demo by comparing O to I transformations. Key observation from demo 3: O[i][j] for j<10, i<10 = I[i][j] (block preserved), and outside it's periodic extension. Check demo 1: is O a 2x2 tiling of the input where the zero-quadrant issue... demo 1 has no zeros. O 28x28. Is O[14+i][14+j] = I[i][j]? Row 14 (i=0): [4]*14 vs I[0]=[4]*14 ✓ for first 14! Tail of row 14: 2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4 vs I[0][14..] doesn't exist. Hmm but if we treat I as cyclic (torus): I[0][j mod 14] = all 4s for j=14-27. O row 14 tail ≠ 4s. ✗.

But maybe tiling isn't aligned at 14. Check O[i][j] = I[i'][j'] with (i',j') = ((i+α) mod 14, (j+β) mod 14) globally? Earlier attempt with affine found best mism 474 etc — worst. Let me instead search: assume O = I tiled with period n but with each tile being I transformed by a symmetry, varying per tile. Or O = 2x2 arrangement of transformed copies: TL=?, TR=I, BL=I, BR=?

TL of demo1: rows 0-13, cols 0-13 of O: row 0 = all 4s = I row 0! row 1 = [1]*27+[4]: O TL row 1 = first 14: [1]*13+[4] = I row 1 ✓!! row 2: O TL row 2 = [9]*12+[1,4] = I row 2 ✓. So TL == I too?! Then what's different? O is 28x28; TL = I, TR = I (from earlier), BL = I, BR = ??? BR = rows 14-27, cols 14-27. Row 14 cols 14-27 = tail [2,9,7,9,...]. BR row 0 = [2,9,7,9,6,7,8,1,2,9,1,4].
